proof_summary: Take the composite square \(n=p^2=16843^2\): a finite modular inverse-sum computation gives \(v_p(H_{p-1})\ge3\), while splitting \(H_{p^2-1}\) according to divisibility by \(p\) and pairing \(j\) with \(p^2-j\) gives \(v_p(H_{p^2-1})\ge2\). The identity \(H_{p^2-2}-1=H_{p^2-1}-p^2/(p^2-1)\) then shows that \(p^2\) divides the numerator-minus-denominator of \(H_{p^2-2}\), so the relevant gcd is all of \(p^2\) although \(p^2\) is composite.
